Society & Human Rights.title: Chimpanzees once used for vaccine research get health checks as part of long-term care
Society & Human Rights.text:
In this handout photo released by Humane World for Animals, a chimpanzee formerly used in research receives a comprehensive health check at a retirement sanctuary for chimpanzees, in Bapakwali, Liberia, on Aug. 25, 2026. (Humane World for Animals via AP)2026-09-05T09:48:07Z
                                        ABUJA, Nigeria (AP) — A group of chimpanzees that were once used for hepatitis B vaccine experiments in laboratories have received health checks at their new home in Liberia, in hopes of giving them a second chance at a normal life.The West African chimpanzees received checks ranging from teeth cleaning to X-rays and pedicure at the Humane World for Animals’ Second Chance Chimpanzee Refuge in central Liberia, Liliana Pacheco Ricote, director of the sanctuary, told The Associated Press.More than 400 of the chimpanzees had been used by American researchers in Liberia in the hepatitis B vaccine experiments from the 1970s until early 2000s, Ricote said, many of them captured in the wild as infants.Liberia has the second-highest number of chimpanzees in West Africa, after Guinea. The West African chimpanzees are classified as critically endangered species because of their rapidly declining numbers.
    
        
    

“They were used in very invasive research … (and) went through a lot of experiments and pain,” Ricote said.Humane World for Animals said that in 2015, it assumed permanent responsibility for 60 of the chimpanzees that were remaining at the end of the research program. The chimps now mostly live at the sanctuary on a series of mangrove forest-covered islands.The checks carried out under anesthetic gave the chimpanzees head-to-toe exams to assess their long-term health, detect any early signs of disease and tailor care plans for individuals as they age, Humane World for Animals said in a statement to the AP. 

The tests included dental examination, the heart, lungs and nervous system as well as blood. They get booster vaccinations and fingernail trims, it said, adding that plans are in place to carry out the checks on the remaining ones.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
“The health checks are a vital part of caring for these chimpanzees who have been through so much,” said Belen Perez Hernando, the sanctuary’s veterinarian.The extent of the impact of the experiments on the chimps, whose average age is 30 to 35, is unclear, as findings from the assessments are yet to be concluded. However, “for those who were under experiments, you could still feel the hurt and the pain that they went through,” Ricote said.
    
        
    

“Seeing how much they hurt about what we’ve done, it gives me a lot of pleasure … to give them this second chance to live with dignity the life that they deserve,” she added.

Society & Human Rights.title: Serbian club Red Star Belgrade fined by UEFA for fan chants in honor of war criminal Ratko Mladic
Society & Human Rights.text:
A mural shows former Bosnian Serb wartime general Ratko Mladic in Belgrade, Serbia, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Darko Vojinovic)2026-09-05T08:59:37Z
                                        NYON, Switzerland (AP) — Serbian soccer club Red Star Belgrade was fined by UEFA for fans chanting in honor of convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, who died on the day of a Europa League game last week.Red Star fans chanted the name of Mladic, saluted him and showed a banner thanking and praising him at a 5-1 loss at Czech club Viktoria Plzeň on Aug. 27.Mladic was the Bosnian Serb commander who oversaw the massacre of more than 8,000 Muslims in Srebrenica in 1995 and other war crimes. Mladic died in The Hague where he was serving a life sentence for genocide. He was 84.UEFA said late Friday its judges fined Red Star 90,000 euros ($104,500) for charges including chants not fit for a sports event plus “racist and/or discriminatory behavior.”Red Star also was banned from selling tickets to fans for its next away game in a UEFA competition. That will apply when the Serbian champion visits Swiss club Lugano in the third-tier Conference League.UEFA deferred another away tickets ban on Red Star for a two-year probationary period.Red Star, the European champion in 1991, has a long track record of disciplinary sanctions from UEFA for misconduct by fans including racist slurs against Roma people.___See AP’s full soccer coverage here

Society & Human Rights.title: Masked men block traffic to UK’s port of Dover, site of past anti-immigrant protests
Society & Human Rights.text:
Students who fell ill allegedly due to food poisoning after consuming free meals at their school receive medical treatment at a hospital in Sidoarjo, East Java, Indonesia, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Jusuf Aydin)2026-09-05T09:11:24Z
                                        LONDON (AP) — A group of masked men blocked the entrance to Britain’s busiest ferry port on Saturday. Police said they were “engaging with the protesters.”The Port of Dover said all traffic in and out “is stopped due to an ongoing public order incident.”Footage on social media showed several dozen men in black, their faces covered, standing across a major road near the port.It was not immediately clear what they were demanding.The National Highways agency said the protests caused a 4-mile (6.4-kilometer) traffic jam, causing delays of up to 45 minutes.P&O Ferries, which runs services between Dover and Calais in France, said its boats were running on schedule, and passengers who missed their ferry would be offered the next available crossing.Dover, about 70 miles (110 kilometers) southeast of London, has been the site of previous anti-immigrant protests focused on migrants who cross the Channel from France in small boats. Some politicians, including Nigel Farage of hard-right party Reform UK, have seized on the issue. He branded the asylum seekers “an invasion” in a Friday speech.
    
        
    

The Labour Party government says stepped-up law enforcement cooperation between Britain and France has helped reduce the number of people making the crossing this year by more than 40% compared to 2025.Mike Tapp, a Labour lawmaker who represents Dover in Parliament, criticized “idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption.”


    
        




    


“I bet if you asked any one of those ‘protesters’ they wouldn’t know small boat crossing are down by 40% and we are working hard to fix the mess,” he wrote on Facebook on Saturday. “Go home, enjoy your weekend/get a job.”

A drone view shows a damaged residential building along the swollen Trishuli River in the aftermath of flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district, Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Rajesh Kumar Singh)2026-09-05T08:15:29Z
                                        KATHMANDU, Nepal (AP) — Rescuers in Nepal pulled a Chinese national alive from a hydropower tunnel on Saturday, according to a social media post by the country’s prime minister’s office.The latest rescue brings the total to three workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. Two Nepalese workers were rescued from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower plant on Friday.Nepal army said the man was pulled alive from a 225-meter tunnel (about 738 feet) and is undergoing a health assessment. Images showed him being evacuated by helicopter, with an army medic checking on him during the flight.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects across Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in various tunnels, according to authorities.At least 1,300 people were killed in the Aug. 26 floods, which were likely caused by a glacier collapse, and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.

Climate & Environment.text: The catastrophic flooding in July 2021 claimed the lives of more than 200 people in Germany and Belgium. The high death toll makes it clear that hazard mapping and risk communication must be improved urgently. Researchers at the University of Potsdam, the Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, the University of Louvain and Johns Hopkins University analyzed the locations and specific circumstances of 224 deaths. Their findings show that many occurred outside the officially mapped flood hazard zones and that older people were particularly affected. The work is published in the journal Earth's Future.

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Russian attacks kill 4 in Ukraine as Moscow and Kyiv prepare for visit by US envoys
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
A local resident wears a gas mask as he rides a bicycle past a partially destroyed warehouse after a Russian drone attack in Brovary on the outskirts of Kyiv, Ukraine, Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Francisco Seco)2026-09-05T09:04:34Z
                                        Russian attacks killed four people in Ukraine overnight, as Moscow and Kyiv await the arrival of U.S. envoys to begin a new push for peace in the Kremlin’s 4 1/2-year-old invasion.The planned visit by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also U.S. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, is hoped to revive peace talks amid escalating aerial attacks by both sides.The air war between Russia and Ukraine has intensified as troops have struggled to make progress along the 1,250-kilometer (775-mile) front line. Russia has recently been using fast-flying, jet-powered drones, and the recurring wail of air-raid sirens has become part of daily life in Kyiv. The strikes come despite a message from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy Friday saying that Ukraine would halt air attacks during Witkoff and Kushner’s visit and urging Moscow to do the same.
    
        
    

“Just as we did during previous diplomatic visits by the American side, we will ensure the normal functioning of Russian airspace so that the negotiators can arrive safely,” Zelenskyy said in a post on social media. “There will be no airstrikes from our side, and Russia must do the same, ensuring there are no airstrikes from its side for the time needed to hold these talks and handle the logistical matters related to this American visit.”Russian attacks killed four people and wounded five more at an industrial facility in Ukraine’s southern Dnipropetrovsk region, local military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha said. A 62-year-old man was also wounded and several private homes and an apartment building were damaged in a separate attack on the region’s Nikopol district, he said.


    
        




    


In a statement Saturday, Russia’s Ministry of Defense said it had carried out strikes on two metallurgical plants in the region, describing them as “major suppliers of metal products for Ukraine’s military production.”

Russian forces also repeatedly struck a shopping center in the southern Mykolaiv region with drones overnight, damaging retail premises and sparking fires, Ukraine’s state emergency services said. A 72-year-old man and a 17-year-old girl were hurt.

Armed Conflict & Security.title: Months after ceasefire, Israel and Hezbollah battle over a strategic hill in Lebanon
Armed Conflict & Security.text:
An Israeli tank moves past a convoy of the United Nations peacekeeping forces in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in southern Lebanon, as seen from northern Israel on June 26, 2026. (AP Photo/Leo Correa, File)2026-09-05T06:35:26Z
                                        BEIRUT (AP) — Since a ceasefire went into effect between Israel and Hezbollah more than two months ago, fighting has stopped in much of Lebanon, but not on a strategic hill overlooking parts of a main southern city.In recent weeks, Ali Taher hill has been the scene of daily shelling and airstrikes by Israel’s military. Hezbollah, a militant group backed by Iran, has repeatedly attacked Israeli forces in the area with drones.The United States, which is mediating talks between Lebanon and Israel, had wanted Hezbollah to hand over the hill to the Lebanese army as part of larger plan to disarm the militant group and dismantle its infrastructure. But Hezbollah has refused.Lebanon and Israel reached a framework agreement in June stating Israel will withdraw from Lebanon as Hezbollah is disarmed. The militant group was not a party to the negotiations and has rejected calls to disarm in areas north of the Litani river, which is where Ali Taher is located.
    
        
    

A full-on battle over this hill near the city of Nabatiyeh could escalate fighting across the country, and unrest in Lebanon complicates efforts to resolve the war in Iran.On Thursday night, Israel’s military announced it had taken “operational control” of Ali Taher and a network of tunnels beneath it that Hezbollah uses to shelter its fighters and weapons. It is unclear how far Israel’s control extends. Just before Israel’s announcement, its air force was still targeting the hill, according to Lebanese state media.There has been no official statement from Hezbollah since Israel’s announcement. 


    
        




    


US pushes Lebanon to pressure HezbollahHezbollah firmly rejected a proposal from the Lebanese government to hand over Ali Taher to the country’s army. It fears Israel would then seize control of the hill from the Lebanese army and then demand the handover of more territory.Israel had occupied Ali Taher for 18 years before it withdrew from Lebanon in 2000.
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
The hill has a strategic location overlooking several villages as well as main roads leading to Nabatiyeh. Losing full control of it would disrupt Hezbollah’s presence and supply lines in the area.
    
        
    

The Israeli military says the site is also important to Hezbollah because of tunnels it built there, with funding from Iran.Israel said in its statement Thursday that the hill housed underground command centers, weapons storage rooms, generators, living quarters, showers and a kitchen. Israel said it cleared Ali Taher of Hezbollah fighters and was working to “neutralize underground infrastructure sites.”

Hezbollah legislator Ihab Hamadeh questioned why the Israeli military was still attacking the hill if it was really in control of the area, according to the Arabic-language version of Russia’s state-funded news outlet Sputnik. An Associated Press photographer who visited the nearby village of Kfar Rumman on Friday saw no sign of Israeli military presence on the hill. The hill, topped with a shrine to a Muslim scholar, sits north of the Litani river, which has become the de facto boundary of the area captured by Israel since its latest war with Hezbollah began in early March. 
    
        
    

Fighting in the area has heated up in recent weeksIsrael has been conducting military operations around Ali Taher since July, said Nasser Khdour, a Middle East researcher at the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, or ACLED, a U.S.-based group that tracks conflicts around the world. Hezbollah official Mahmoud Qamati told a Lebanese podcaster in late August that the group’s fighters were repelling attempts by Israeli troops to take Ali Taher. But he, and others, downplayed the significance of the site should Israel take it.“Ali Taher is important, but if it is lost it does not mean the end of Hezbollah,” Qamati said.In mid-August, Israel carried out a series of airstrikes on southern Lebanon that it described as retaliation for a Hezbollah drone attack on Ali Taher that seriously wounded three soldiers. The Israeli strikes, which killed 11 people, including women and children, were the deadliest since the U.S.-brokered ceasefire went into effect in late June.On Aug. 27, Israel carried out a series of airstrikes, killing one person and wounding six, after the military said Hezbollah fired two explosive drones at Israeli troops in the area. Hezbollah did not claim responsibility for any of the attacks.
    
        
    

Lebanon says Israel is hindering its armyLebanon’s Deputy Prime Minister Tarek Mitri told an Arab TV station in late August that the Lebanese army was ready to take over Ali Taher.He accused Israel of blocking the army due to its own political considerations ahead of Israeli national elections on Oct. 27.“The problem is not in the Lebanese army’s readiness but in Israel’s stance,” he said.Lebanese and Israeli officials are set to meet for negotiations in Rome later this month. Meanwhile, Hezbollah, which has always refused to speak directly to the U.S., appears to be changing its policy after the major setbacks it has suffered during its wars with Israel since 2024.A Lebanese official told The Associated Press that indirect contacts are going on between the U.S. and Hezbollah, but refused to give any details. He spoke on condition of anonymity in line with regulations.
    
        
    

The U.S. ambassador to Lebanon, Michel Issa, said recently that Washington is ready to speak with Hezbollah if the group agrees to disarm. Still, Hezbollah is not likely to take any move forward regarding talks with the U.S. without a green light from its main backer, Iran. While talks with the U.S. over their war have stalled, Iran has sought guarantees that Israel will halt its attacks on Hezbollah as part of any permanent deal.Capture of Ali Taher could lead Israel to other Hezbollah strongholdsThe capture of Ali Taher would open the way to Nabatiyeh and also lead to the nearby Apple Province and Rihan Mountain, where Hezbollah has been building up its presence since the late 1990s.Israeli leaders have repeatedly pledged to leave troops in Lebanon and threatened to escalate military pressure until Hezbollah disarms.“Israeli control of the area is an operational and military setback for Hezbollah,” said Khdour of ACLED. He said clearing these sites helps Israel protect towns in the northern part of its country, and increases pressure on Hezbollah.“This will strengthen Israel’s position in any future negotiations over its withdrawal,” said Khdour.

Geopolitics & Diplomacy.title: Philippines Vice President Duterte posts bail after arrest order for alleged threats against Marcos
Geopolitics & Diplomacy.text:
Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte shows a document to reporters at the Quezon city justice hall Saturday, Sept. 5, 2026, after an arrest warrant was issued on charges that she publicly threatened to have the president and two other people assassinated. (AP Photo/Aaron Favila)2026-09-05T06:36:34Z
                                        MANILA, Philippines (AP) — Philippines Vice President Sara Duterte posted bail Saturday after an order was issued for her arrest the previous day on charges that she publicly threatened to arrange the assassination of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and two other people. Emerging in a black outfit from Quezon City Regional Trial Court in Metro Manila, Duterte consoled her supporters, hugging a woman who was sobbing as supporters chanted “Duterte! Duterte!”The vice president, who has denied the allegations, showed a court order lifting the arrest warrant issued by the court Friday and said her lawyers instructed her to keep a copy on hand. She urged journalists to surround her on the way to her car because she did not feel safe. “If possible please go with me, because I do not feel safe with all these police personnel who are harassing those at my home, harassing me since 2023,” Duterte said. “What does this administration really want to do with me?”
    
        
    

Paul Lawrence Lim, one of her attorneys, said court staff took Duterte’s fingerprints and she posted 360,000 pesos bail ($5,740) for three counts of grave threats. After the arrest order was issued Friday, he said Duterte would fight the charges.“She has no intention of evading the law and will continue to exercise all her legal remedies,” he said in a statement.


    
        




    


Case based on comments during online news conferenceThe case is seen as part of a high-stakes political showdown pitting Duterte against Marcos. A conviction may permanently disqualify her from holding public office and prohibit her from seeking the presidency in 2028, when Marcos’s six-year term ends.The charges stem from an alleged threat Duterte, 48, made during a 2024 online news conference. She said she would have Marcos, his wife and then-House of Representatives Speaker Martin Romualdez killed by an assassin if she herself was killed as their political disputes escalated. 
    
        
            
                
                    
    
    


    

  

  
    Read More 
  
  

    
    
    
  

    
        
    

                
            
        
    
The vice president warned during the event that her threat was not a joke. Duterte later said she was expressing concern for her own safety and not threatening Marcos as the remarks set off a criminal investigation and national security concerns.The House of Representatives, which is dominated by Marcos’ allies, voted overwhelmingly in May to impeach Duterte over allegations of unexplained wealth, misuse of confidential state funds and the online news conference threats. The Philippine Senate, acting as an impeachment court, opened her televised trial in July.
    
        
    

Former political partners turned rivalsMarcos and Duterte were running mates in the 2022 elections in an alliance that combined two of the country’s most formidable political dynasties. Marcos is the son of former President Ferdinand Marcos Sr., who held the office from the 1960s to the 1980s, including a period of repression and martial law. The vice president is the daughter of former President Rodrigo Duterte, the predecessor to the current President Marcos.

Marcos and Sara Duterte also have contrasting geopolitical leanings. Marcos has expanded defense engagements with the United States, a treaty ally of the Philippines, as his administration stood up to China’s increasingly aggressive actions in the disputed South China Sea. Economy & Markets.title: Wall Street week ahead: The market focuses on key inflation updates
Economy & Markets.text:
Options trader Marty Handler works on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, Thursday, Aug. 27, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura)2026-09-05T08:00:08Z
                                        NEW YORK (AP) — Wall Street will get several important updates about inflation this week.On Thursday, the U.S. will release its August report for inflation at the wholesale level, called the Producer Price Index, or the PPI. It provides details on prices for businesses before they pass along the costs to consumers.On Friday, the U.S. will release its better-known Consumer Price Index, for August. The CPI is closely watched and provides details on price changes for specific grocery items, furniture, and clothing, among other categories. It also details price changes for services ranging from car maintenance to travel and restaurant dining.The reports will help give Wall Street and the Federal Reserve a clearer picture of inflation’s direction. The rate of inflation remains above 3% and is squeezing households and businesses. Inflation is also outpacing wage growth, putting more strain on households.
    
        
    

Rising energy prices because of the U.S. war with Iran have been fueling inflation. Shipping has been stifled in the Strait of Hormuz, through which about 20% of the world’s oil supply flowed prior to the war. That has pushed prices for gasoline and shipped goods higher.Ongoing tariff conflicts between the U.S. and most of the world also threatens to send prices higher.


    
        




    


The Fed has been holding its benchmark interest rate steady, but Wall Street expects it to raise the rate at least once this year to help fight inflation. The central bank’s stated goal is to cool inflation to a rate of 2%.

Art & Culture.title: How This 88-Year-Old Whisky Inspired Daniel Arsham’s New Artworks
Art & Culture.text: Daniel Arsham’s latest zen garden performance could be the makings of your great-grandchildren’s favorite whisky. Four dancers move through a circular bed of barley at S50 in Seongsu, Seoul, sweeping, raking, and gliding through the sea of grains in meditative gestures. While this barley likely won’t hit the mill, the “Dawn Of Our Spirit” experience was inspired by traditional whisky-making, culminating in its last act: the reveal of The Balvenie’s 88-year-old Single Scotch Malt.Distilled in 1931 and bottled in 2019 by Malt Master Kelsey McKechnie, The Balvenie’s oldest (and rarest) edition leads its new 1931 Collection. When it came time to debut the bottle during Frieze Seoul, the label tapped Arsham for a sculptural casing and companion performance that embodies its generations-long devotion to craft, technique, and tradition, while also feeling artistically at home.The story behind the bottle begins with Arsham’s first trip to the distillery in Speyside, Scotland, said to be the heart of whisky country. “One of the things that struck me was the handmade quality of everything. It's technical, but very craft in a way, so I pulled out a lot of materials I saw.” Arsham said, sitting across from Hypebeast at The Distiller’s Library inside the Shilla Hotel. “We went through a lot of different processes around the [bottle’s] design,” with several “experimental” mockups behind him. “In the end, the preciousness of that liquid really needs to be considered.”The liquid itself lay in a hand-blown crystal decanter detailed with 18-karat gold gilding, a stopper made from a decommissioned copper still, and a neck taking after the “Balvenie Ball,” the unique still shape which gives the whisky its famed honeyed flavor. Arsham also created the architecture housing the form. Its face features eight fluid layers of hand-patinated copper, evoking textures and hues found throughout the still safe, while 88 thinly layered sections of oak on the back refer to the European oak sherry butt where it was first poured. “It’s the whisky when it’s moving through time,” he explained. “When you look at the sculpture, it's moving through the copper, into the wood, and then into your glass.”Beyond closing the cask of the 88-year-old, 1931 was a defining year for the label, which then opened its Home Malt Floor, still in operation. In today’s whisky game, the labor-intensive floor malting is seen as old-school. But for The Balvenie, it’s the bedrock to its heritage craft and timeless taste.From initial whiffs of earthy barley to Sukyung Yoo’s choreography, which oscillates between lyrical and sharp, intense movements, the collaborative performance takes you from Seoul to Speyside upon walking through the doors of S50. “It’s still a very handmade process,” said Arsham, who directed the performance. “Sometimes we lose a little bit of that seeing it just on a shelf or having it at home. We tried together to bring some of that into the experience and tell that story.”Craft, material, and the survival of time are key to understanding Arsham’s practice, notably through his self-coined “fictional archaeology,” making The Balvenie collaboration a natural fit. His series, Eroded Classical Sculpture and Zen Garden, most clearly echoed through the project, explore questions of memory, traditions, and how they materialize and transform even hundreds of years on.“In whisky, nothing happens overnight,” said McKechnie, the current Malt Master overseeing nearly a century of inventory. “The fruits of today's craftspeople might not be tasted for generations.”“Being able to release an 88-year-old really reaffirms this to everyone at the distillery, that all the hard work that we're putting in today is a real testament to persistence and patience. That's something I think Daniel understands beautifully.”But the 88-year-old isn't just a record-breaker for the house; it's the oldest whisky ever released. When it came time to announce, however, carrying the new world record was just part of the story. “At The Balvenie, we are always in charge of our own destiny,” McKechnie said. “I love the thought of us doing something that changes the landscape of Scotch whisky. We've done it before. I relish the opportunity to do it again.”Following its Seoul debut, the “Dawn Of Our Spirit” performance will make stops in New York, Shanghai, and Taipei. Entertainment.title: Moto Guzzi’s renovated Lake Como headquarters welcomes a pilgrimage of motorcycle-bound aficionados
Entertainment.text:
Visitors look at the Moto Guzzi motorcycle engines on display at the museum during the Moto Guzzio pening inaugurating its completely redeveloped historic factory and new museum as the motorcycle maker celebrates its 105th anniversary, in Mandello del Lario, Thursday, Sept. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Luca Bruno)2026-09-05T09:47:05Z
                                        MANDELLO DEL LARIO, Italy (AP) — After extensive renovation by the Italian motorcycle manufacturer Moto Guzzi, aficionados this year had fresh reasons for a pilgrimage to the lakeside spot where their beloved two-cylinder bikes are hand-built. Thousands of Moto Guzzi riders pulled up Saturday for an annual gathering and informal ride along the winding lakeside roads. They started arriving on Thursday for the unveiling of the headquarters, new museum and expanded factory on the shores of northern Italy’s Lake Como.The headquarters, nestled between a mountainside and the lakeshore, received an additional 5,500 square meters (nearly 60,000 square feet) for factory space and the museum that honors the iconic brand that has been owned by Vespa-maker Piaggio since 2004. Works took five years and cost more than 50 million euros ($58 million).
    
        
    

Timothy Bennett, who lives in the U.S. state of Georgia, was making his second trip to the headquarters after attending a toned-down 100th anniversary celebration during the pandemic. His first Moto Guzzi — made distinctive by its dual cylinders projecting from either side of the bike — was an 850-T, and now he owns a 2018 California 1400 Touring.“I’ve owned a Moto Guzzi since my 20s,” said Bennett, 58. “The first time I saw one in a magazine, I thought it looked very interesting. And then I went ahead and saved up some money and bought a used one, and fell in love.”


    
        




    


This year, Bennett and other visitors to the World Guzzi Days could peek through new observation points to see workers hand-assembling the motorcycles, just as they have for 105 years. The company prides itself on its processes.

“Moto Guzzi is handmade, it is an artisanal product, it’s a piece of art,” said Matteo Boddi, head of manufacturing for the Piaggio Group. “And we never substitute automation for this core part. Automation is for safety and for sustainability.”The new factory includes the addition of an automation belt to move parts and engines through the factories and robotics to transport the finished motorcycles for their final test. The factory expansion potentially doubles the maximum production to 30,000 motorcycles a year. 
    
        
    

“We tried to make an accessible place both for passionate motorcyclists and people who are just curious about motorcycles being made in Italy, on Lake Como, and may never even have heard of Moto Guzzi before,” said U.S. architect Greg Lynn.

Entertainment.title: Nike Wraps the Air Force 1 in GORE-TEX and Vibram for a Winterized "Baroque Brown" Build
Entertainment.text: Name: Nike Air Force 1 Low GORE-TEX “Baroque Brown”Colorway: Baroque Brown/Speed Yellow-University Red-Shadow BrownSKU: HV5953-200MSRP: $150 USDRelease Date: TBC 2026The Nike Air Force 1 Low GORE-TEX "Baroque Brown" takes one of Nike's most familiar silhouettes and reworks it for colder, wetter days. Set for a 2026 release, the shoe layers weatherproofing and a grippier outsole onto the standard AF1, turning an all-year staple into a purpose-built winter option.The upper is where the seasonal intent shows first. Most of it is finished in Baroque Brown leather, with black Swooshes, heel tabs, lining, and midsole cutting through the tone. GORE-TEX is built into the leather for weather protection, and the product images show the material beading water rather than soaking it in. Brown rope laces and a thicker tongue reinforce the winter-ready feel, while small yellow GORE-TEX tags near the collar provide one of the only bright accents on an otherwise muted build.A metal lace dubrae carries another GORE-TEX callout, and Nike Air branding is embossed into the black heel tabs, keeping the back of the shoe clean without introducing extra color. It is a restrained execution that leans on texture and hardware rather than loud graphics to signal the technical upgrade.Underfoot is the clearest departure from a standard Air Force 1. Nike drops the usual outsole in favor of a Vibram unit with a more aggressive traction pattern, aimed at the same slick, cold conditions the upper is built for. Black rubber wraps the outer edges while University Red fills most of the center, and yellow Vibram branding at the midfoot and lateral heel ties back to the GORE-TEX tag up top.Taken together, the changes reframe the AF1 as more than a seasonal colorway. By pairing a waterproof membrane with a purpose-built Vibram sole, Nike positions the "Baroque Brown" pair as a genuine all-weather version of a shoe that usually trades on year-round wearability, giving the silhouette a functional reason to exist in the depths of winter.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Pas Normal Studios' Fall/Winter 2026 Cycling Collections Split the Cold Into Three Riding Mindsets
Entertainment.text: SummaryPas Normal Studios frames its Fall/Winter 2026 season around the idea that riders share the same conditions but train for personal reasonsThree collections cover racing, gravel exploration and relaxed everyday performance, each built on its own technical constructionA seasonal color palette pulls from the textile traditions of mountain communities where craft blends artistry with functionPas Normal Studios has unveiled its Fall/Winter 2026 cycling collections, uniting Mechanism, Escapism and Essential under a single seasonal narrative titled "Same Season. Different Reasons." The Copenhagen brand treats winter riding as one shared commitment approached through different motivations, then engineers a distinct garment system for each: dedicated racing, gravel adventure and understated daily riding.Mechanism is the race-fit line, and for FW26 it grows into a fuller cold-weather system. The centerpiece Mechanism Thermal Jacket is built from a three-layer fabric with a Windtex Pro membrane, pairing a highly breathable 20,000 g/m²/24h construction with 10,000 mm of water resistance. A DWR treatment and ultrasonically welded, taped seams seal out the elements, while a grid-fleece backer handles wicking and insulation without loosening the close race cut. It runs alongside the Thermal Long Sleeve Jersey 2.0, which uses Polartec Power Shield Pro Knit and Power Grid fabrics, and the new Thermal Long Bibs, giving the collection a range that stretches from mild fall days to deep-winter training in rain or snow.Escapism turns toward gravel and terrain beyond the familiar, and its FW26 expansion leads with a rethink of protective outerwear. The new Escapism Hooded Lightweight Jacket uses a three-layer waterproof, lightweight ripstop, with high-stretch, breathable ripstop panels placed to preserve range of motion. Critically taped seams add protection at the points that matter while keeping weight and pack size down, and the hood is cut to sit under a helmet, with elasticated adjustment and ear inserts for fit. Completing the setup are the new Escapism Long Cargo Bibs, made from a textured, rugged fabric meant to survive rough ground.Essential rounds out the season with a looser read on performance, matching technical function to understated styling for everyday rides. Designed to work across transitional weather in both hemispheres, it introduces new colorways across Essential Light and adds more textured seasonal pieces, including the Essential Long Sleeve Jersey, Essential Insulated Gilet and Essential Insulated Jacket, the last group carrying Polartec Alpha insulation panels for lightweight warmth as conditions shift. Tying the three collections together is that shared color story, drawn from mountain communities whose textile craft has long merged vibrant color, intricate pattern and texture with practical purpose.The Pas Normal Studios Fall/Winter 2026 collections are available now online, via Pas Normal Studios retail locations and selected wholesale partners.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: L’Épée 1839 Transforms a Soccer Ball Into an 8-Day Kinetic Clock Sculpture
Entertainment.text: SummaryL’Épée 1839 unveils “The Football” kinetic table clock at Geneva Watch Days 2026.Features a 1:1 scale truncated icosahedron design constructed from 882 individual hand-finished components.Houses an 8-day in-house mechanical movement across four finishes limited to 99 pieces each.Unveiled at Geneva Watch Days 2026, “The Football” by L’Épée 1839 marks the Swiss Manufacture's latest kinetic sculpture. Joining the LVMH group, the brand expands its sports-inspired lineup into the world of soccer. The timepiece draws inspiration from the geometry of the truncated icosahedron - specifically the 1962 Telstar satellite and the 1970 Telstar match ball produced by adidas - featuring an architectural layout made of 12 pentagons and 20 hexagons built to a 1:1 scale of an official soccer ball.Comprising 882 individual components, the kinetic sculpture is divided into two interlocking modules that house an 8-day in-house mechanical movement. The openworked skeletal framework reveals its internal gear train and escapement at the base, creating a dynamic visual contrast between traditional haute horlogerie and athletic industrial design. Time is read through rotating discs visible through the geometric cutouts, while the movement is wound via a custom key positioned at the top of the sculpture.L’Épée 1839 offers "The Football" in four distinct surface finishes: full gold-plated, full palladium-plated and two two-tone variants featuring either black or gold numerals. Each finish is strictly limited to 99 pieces, capping total production across the collection at 396 units. Designed for high-end table clock collectors, every individual component undergoes hand-finishing with alternating polished and satin-brushed textures. For more information, head over to L’Épée 1839's official website.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: Ib Kamara Exits Off-White & The Met Cancels John Galliano Exhibition in This Week's Top Fashion News
Entertainment.text: SummaryIb Kamara mutually steps down from his creative director role at Off-White™, while The Met officially cancels its controversial Spring 2026 John Galliano exhibition.Stone Island taps cultural fixtures like fakemink for its latest campaign, and a Beijing-based designer transforms the Air Jordan 1 for women.YOSHIDA & Co. brings a five-day PORTER limited store to New York, and Sandy Liang reflects on a decade of design in her new monograph.Ib Kamara Exits Off-White™Ib Kamara and Off-White™ mutually parted ways, concluding the designer's tenure as creative director. Kamara, a close collaborator of the late Virgil Abloh, formally took the helm in Spring 2022. The CEO of Bluestar Alliance, Joey Gabbay, thanked Kamara in an official statement: "We are deeply grateful for Ib’s vision, creativity, and the remarkable energy he brought to Off-White throughout his tenure. Ib’s contributions have been instrumental in shaping and evolving the brand, and we sincerely thank him for his dedication and lasting impact.” During his run, Kamara spearheaded notable milestones, including Off-White™’s first New York fashion show in Brooklyn and the launch of the more accessible L/AB c/o Off-White line. The house has not yet named a successor.The Met Cancels John Galliano ExhibitionThe Metropolitan Museum of Art officially cancels its planned Spring 2026 Costume Institute exhibition, “John Galliano: Horizons,” following widespread backlash regarding the designer’s 2011 racist remarks. In a joint statement, Galliano, Anna Wintour, and curator Andrew Bolton confirmed the mutual decision not to proceed. Galliano expressed regret and took accountability for his past words, while Wintour offered her full support for the cancellation. John Galliano wrote an extended remark, saying, “After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” he said. “I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it.”Fakemink and Skepta's First Collaboration Is in the New Stone Island CampaignStone Island’s ongoing “Community as a Form of Research” campaign returns with a new roster of cultural tastemakers. The latest visual series stars fakemink, Skepta, Stephen Graham, 3House, Samir Bantal, Monika Sprüth, and Jia Zhang-Ke. Photographed by David Sims and styled by Max Pearmain, the cast members don a range of Stone Island outerwear, from fakemink's glossy resin-treated jacket to Stephen Graham's monochromatic rubberized lambskin piece, answering a questionnaire curated by Hans Ulrich Obrist.Take an Inside Look at 'Dressing Up,' Sandy Liang's First Rizzoli MonographNew York designer Sandy Liang chronicles over a decade of her namesake label in Dressing Up: Sandy Liang, a 276-page hardcover monograph published by Rizzoli. "Sharing my life through my work feels intuitive for me – one does not feel complete without the other. This scrapbook of memories captures a decade of the brand through that lens," Liang shared in the official release. Sourcing heavily from previously unpublished personal film and iPhone photography, the book acts as an intimate scrapbook detailing Liang's runway moments, downtown New York inspirations, and her signature nostalgia-driven aesthetic. The project features contributions from creative director Ava Nirui and stylist Dean DiCriscio.The Air Jordan 1 Was Reimagined by Eight Finalists & This One WonBeijing-based designer Syn Zhuang wins the inaugural Jordan Design Studio program, a global initiative challenging creatives to reimagine the classic Air Jordan 1. Selected at Jordan’s “The One” event in Shanghai, Zhuang’s concept strips back the iconic silhouette to cater specifically to female wearers. Her design features a softer, rounded toe box and a transformable suede collar that reveals a backward Swoosh when worn up, offering a versatile and comfortable take on the famously sleek basketball sneaker. On her personal Instagram page, Zhuang shared more insight: “A classic doesn’t have to be one fixed form. It can exist in different ways, to reach different people. I wanted this shoe to offer a little sense of ease — not laziness, not giving up, just a feeling that it’s okay to loosen up and be yourself.”PORTER Is Back in NYC With a Five-Day Pop-UpYOSHIDA & Co. returns to New York with the PORTER LIMITED STORE, a five-day pop-up in SOHO running through September 6. The temporary space showcases Japanese craftsmanship across three of the company's brands: PORTER, POTR, and L.L. Shoppers can expect a curated selection of backpacks, shoulder bags, and totes, alongside collaborative capsules with Aurel Schmidt and HELLO KITTY. The pop-up also offers the new YOSHIDA & Co. 90 Anniversary BOOK and features custom fixtures built specifically for the New York location.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: norda and Black Diamond Enter a New Era of Alpine Performance
Entertainment.text: In an era defined by collaboration, the partnerships that truly resonate feel inevitable. norda and Black Diamond are exactly that: two brands united by a shared obsession with performance, coming together through the all-new norda 000 silhouette to redefine what alpine exploration can look like.norda, the performance footwear brand built on advanced material innovation, and Black Diamond Equipment, a global leader in mountain sports equipment and apparel, have entered a long-term partnership, bringing together their respective expertise in footwear and mountain equipment. Anchored in an all-new set of trail-ready products, the collection draws on both brands' experience to create the highest-quality gear possible, combining advanced technology with decades of mountain expertise.Hypebeast wanted to learn more about the collaboration, speaking with Adam John, norda’s Creative Director, and Dan Rowe, Special Projects and Design Lead at Black Diamond, about how the partnership began and how it ultimately came to life.What sparked the initial ideas for this collaboration — where did this idea come from?Dan Rowe: The origins of this partnership began at the athlete level, with admiration for Joe Grant in the way he chooses to interact with trails. While he has a decorated past in traditional racing, his movement through the mountains has evolved into something more than numbers and data. Following his journey offers a rare lens into the spirit that drives us outside in the first place, and Black Diamond is a rare brand that caters to the spirited yet serious.How did both Norda and Black Diamond’s DNA show up in the design?Adam John: We built this partnership from the ground up—quite literally. Rather than take an existing shoe model and co-brand it, we created a brand-new shoe that dictated the type of movement we wanted the partnership to convey. The result is the norda x Black Diamond 000, a shoe for long days that can handle highly variable and uneven terrain. Black Diamond's equipment followed suit: complementary upgrades to existing and new products that support these kinds of journeys. What are some of the shared philosophies and crossovers between the brands?DR: There was an immediate mutual respect between the two design teams and the way each approaches product, but finding the spirit of the collaboration took time and flowed organically. Both brands share a deep connection to the mountains and a belief in creating products that are purposeful, considered, and without anything superfluous. Joe was an important part of that connection, not only as the link between the brands, but through his approach to the mountains and his respect for the beauty of running in natural places.Were there any technical details, materials, or design elements that laid the groundwork for the collaboration? AJ: We create the only trail shoes with purposefully-engineered usage of Dyneema® (the world’s strongest fiber). Thus, from a material standpoint, the goal was to ensure that every technical piece conveyed this ethos of durability. The Distance Pack and Mini Mission Duffel are constructed from a material called Challenge Sailcloth, the Black Diamond analog to Dyneema®. We incorporated the heritage idea through details such as embroidering the Distance Packs and Mini Mission Duffels, while expressing forward-looking innovation through subtle yet never-before-seen details like anodization and laser etching on the trekking poles. The collection delivers a fully integrated kit for efficient alpine movement, with several pieces informed by Black Diamond and norda mountain runner Joe Grant. At its core is the all-new norda 000, designed for high-mountain running, alongside a selection of Black Diamond essentials reimagined with cutting-edge materials, including the Distance 15 Pack, Distance Carbon Z FKT Poles, Mini Mission Duffle 30L, Miniwire Carabiner, T-Shirt, and Cap. The collection is finished in a palette of obsidian and moonstone, accented by soft pink kunzite, drawing inspiration from the minerals found throughout mountain environments.The inaugural norda x Black Diamond collection debuted at Sanglard Sports in Chamonix, France, and is available now at nordarun.com and blackdiamondequipment.com.Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Entertainment.title: PUMA and Hypebeast Hosted “Suede Sessions” in London
Entertainment.text: Under the arches of Waterloo in London, Hypebeast hosted “Suede Sessions” in collaboration with PUMA last week. Inspired by generations of music subcultures connected to the iconic Suede silhouette, the event set out to platform the distinct sounds and eclectic genres shaping the local music scene today.As the first event of its kind, Yussef Dayes was enlisted to unite emerging music artists and a handful of established rappers, musicians, and vocalists through a unique two-part format. Comprising an artist workshop, followed by a live performance later in the day, each activation was hosted by the drummer and composer who brought his genre-blending jazz to the forefront.Dayes kicked off the event with the music-making session. Acting as a creative incubator, the workshop saw the drummer offer advice to help the participants elevate their respective sounds. After collaborating, the workshop culminated in a collective jam as the artists showcased their latest material to the group. A few hours later, the venue was prepared for a live performance headlined by Dayes. In keeping with the graffiti-emblazoned tunnels outside, it was lit up in moody orange lights and featured spray-painted branding on the walls around the main stage. Elsewhere, a pop-up studio was erected for guests to take their own Polaroid portraits. For the first performance, Nepali-American singer-songwriter Parijita set the mood with her ballads, layering deeply melodic vocals and gentle piano notes. London-based music duo ZENA then picked up the tempo, playing a mix of Ethiopian-inspired jazz and dub. Riffing on the melting pot of music styles, Saiming, a rapper hailing from South London, followed on with his blend of grime and neo-jazz. In a crescendo to the night, Dayes took the stage for the final performance. Having recently announced a feature in Wyclef Jean’s new album Q, guests crowded around eager to get up close to listen to his latest music. Over the 30-minute set, he opted for a mix of tracks from his albums, including Black Classical Music, while also going freestyle to honor the playful and experimental edge of London’s music scene. Health & Pandemic.title: Nearly 2,000 fall ill in suspected food poisoning linked to Indonesia’s free school meals program
Health & Pandemic.text:
Students who fell ill allegedly due to food poisoning after consuming free meals at their school receive medical treatment at a hospital in Sidoarjo, East Java, Indonesia, Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Jusuf Aydin)2026-09-05T09:17:33Z
                                        JAKARTA, Indonesia (AP) — Nearly 2,000 people, most of them students, fell ill in suspected food poisoning outbreaks linked to President Prabowo Subianto ’s flagship Free Nutritious Meals program this week, raising fresh concerns about food safety as the government rapidly expands the multibillion-dollar initiative nationwide, officials said Saturday.The incidents, reported between Tuesday and Thursday in East Java, Central Java, West Sumatra, Aceh and South Sulawesi, affected about 1,950 students, teachers and Islamic boarding school pupils who became sick after consuming meals distributed under the government program, known by its Indonesian acronym MBG.The outbreaks are the latest setback for Prabowo’s signature free meals program, which has been rolled out across the archipelago despite repeated food poisoning incidents and corruption allegations.
    
        
    

The largest outbreak was reported in Central Java’s Rembang regency, where 752 students and 25 teachers at State Senior High School 1 Lasem, suffered diarrhea, nausea, vomiting and stomach pain after eating meals provided through the program, according to Rembang Health Office head Ali Syofi’i.In Sidoarjo, East Java, 730 people, most of them students at the Manbaul Hikam Islamic boarding school, were affected in another suspected food poisoning incident linked to the program. Sidoarjo health office chief Lakhsmie Herawati Yuwantina said 706 victims had been discharged and were recovering at home.


    
        




    


Authorities also reported 276 suspected cases involving students and teachers in Agam regency, West Sumatra, where food distribution from the local nutrition service center was suspended pending an investigation. In Aceh’s Bener Meriah regency, 15 elementary school students and a school principal were treated after experiencing dizziness, nausea and other symptoms following a school meal.

Another 152 students from two junior high schools in Tana Toraja, South Sulawesi, were treated at three hospitals after developing symptoms consistent with food poisoning. Regent Zadrak Tombeq ordered hospitals and health centers to prioritize treatment for the victims.
    
        
    

No deaths have been reported, and authorities are investigating the causes of the outbreaks.

The latest incidents add to a growing number of food poisoning cases linked to the program since its launch in January 2025. According to Health Ministry surveillance data as of Sept. 2, food poisoning incidents associated with MBG have affected 50,059 people in 560 cases across 245 districts and cities in 36 provinces.In a hearing with the House’s Commission IX overseeing health issues, National Nutrition Agency chief Sudaryono said internal reviews found that roughly 80% to 90% of previous food poisoning incidents were linked to failures to follow food safety procedures, including rules governing food storage, receipt of ingredients, temperature control and consumption deadlines.“The recent incidents in Sidoarjo, Agam, Rembang and other areas have been a major blow for us,” said Sudaryono, who like many Indonesians uses a single name.He said the agency was tightening oversight of meal providers and reviewing about 27,000 meal distribution centers nationwide. Inspectors have found hundreds of allegedly fictitious facilities, while at least 833 kitchens have been shut down for failing to meet hygiene and sanitation standards.
    
        
    

The free meals program aims to combat malnutrition and reduce childhood stunting by providing meals to nearly 90 million students, toddlers and pregnant women. The initiative, expected to cost about $28 billion through 2029, is a cornerstone of Prabowo’s administration and one of his key campaign promises.

By controlling where in the structure the light is generated, the researchers have reduced the losses that would otherwise limit the amount of light that can be used. Their study is published in the journal Nano Research.

Science & Technology.title: In ant nervous systems, gene expression may drive rescue behavior
Science & Technology.text: Why do some ants help nestmates in distress while others don't? A research team from Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (JGU) and Tel Aviv University addressed this question in a new study. The researchers examined worker ants of the species Cataglyphis niger, some of which had shown rescue behavior while others had not. The results, recently published in the Journal of Experimental Biology, suggest that the key difference lies not in body size, morphology or the animals' energy reserves, but in gene activity in the nervous system.

Science & Technology.title: Shoreline scavenger shows biological effects after eating plastic foam
Science & Technology.text: In a paper published in the journal Marine Pollution Bulletin, researchers at Kyushu University report on what happens when wharf roaches, a common shoreline scavenger, eat expanded polystyrene (EPS). Roaches that fed on EPS showed no significant reduction in lifespan, but their guts displayed altered expression of genes involved in chemical defense, DNA repair and digestion. Analysis of the wharf roach gut microbiome showed little change, but several rare microbes were found only in the EPS-fed specimens.
